title: Research TypeScript-native building blocks to add mcp-agent-style composable MCP agent orchestration as a feature inside Architecture Studio itself
objective: Owner-directed: after ruling out lastmile-ai/mcp-agent as an adoptable dependency (Python, wrong shape/language for coordinating CLI agents), the owner clarified the actual goal is different: build the *capability* mcp-agent demonstrates -- composable MCP-based agent-workflow patterns (router, orchestrator-workers, parallel, evaluator-optimizer) -- as a feature of apps/architecture-studio itself, which is a pure TypeScript web app (confirmed via apps/architecture-studio/project.json: tags lang:typescript, platform:web, no backend target today). Researched TS/JS-native MCP building blocks (the official @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, Vercel AI SDK's MCP client, Mastra, LangGraph.js + @langchain/mcp-adapters, VoltAgent, and others) filtered for permissive licenses given the owner's standing constraint of keeping a future closed-source commercial sale open. Research/documentation only in docs/research/ai-agent-context-and-multi-agent-management-options.md -- no dependency added, no code written, no ADR closed. Must surface, not silently decide, that every candidate found needs a Node-side host process (MCP's stdio transport cannot run in a pure browser SPA) and that live agent-tool-execution is a bigger step than the Studio's current accepted 'initial production slice remains read-only' constraint -- this is a scope-expansion decision for the owner, not a simple dependency pick.
validations: Confirmed via apps/architecture-studio/project.json that the Studio is pure TypeScript/platform:web with no backend/server target -- grounded the research in the app's actual current shape before recommending anything.

Researched via one background pass verifying current license/maturity/runtime facts for @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, Vercel AI SDK's experimental_createMCPClient, Mastra, LangGraph.js + @langchain/mcp-adapters, VoltAgent, and noted (not deep-dived) @inngest/agent-kit and openai/openai-agents-js.

Confirmed the key architectural fact: every candidate needs a Node-side host process (MCP's stdio transport cannot run in a pure browser SPA), and Mastra specifically has a separate source-available 'ee/' enterprise subtree distinct from its Apache-2.0 core.

Added a new 'Part 3' section to docs/research/ai-agent-context-and-multi-agent-management-options.md documenting the candidates, and explicitly surfaced (without deciding) that adding this feature requires (a) giving the Studio a Node-side backend it doesn't have today and (b) crossing the Studio's own already-accepted 'initial production slice remains read-only' constraint -- framed as a scope-expansion decision needing its own task/ADR per DEC-038/DEC-039 and AGENTS.md, not a quiet library pick.
Updated the document's top-level scope note, the 'what this means' synthesis (renamed to 'three live questions'), and the recommended evaluation order to include this as a new numbered step.
No dependency installed, no code written, no ADR closed.
artifacts: docs/research/ai-agent-context-and-multi-agent-management-options.md (added Part 3: TS-native MCP orchestration building blocks for Architecture Studio, plus the Node-backend/read-only-boundary architectural fork this implies)
risks: Research only; no dependency added, no code written, no ADR closed.

Flags a real architectural fork in the road (Studio needs a Node-side backend to host any of these candidates, and live MCP tool execution crosses the existing read-only-slice boundary) rather than deciding it.
